name: DeMeritt Hall
use: Physics and Astronomy (College of Engineering and Physical Sciences)
architect: Architerra, Inc. with Rist-Frost-Shumway; built by Harvey Construction
style: Contemporary brick with glazed curtain-wall stair tower

facts.text: The original 1914 DeMeritt Hall was named for Albert DeMeritt, Durham's state representative who secured its funding; it housed physics, engineering, the School of Architecture and once a temporary dormitory.
The original was demolished in July 2007 and replaced by the current building, completed in 2008.

verdict: Competent 2008 brick physics building with a glazed blue stair tower, a replacement for the 1914 original.
notes: Search snippets say UNH funded it with $18.3M in state KEEP-NH money and an AASHE report called it 'LEED Silver equivalent' (not certified); neither page was opened, so leed is null. Old note 'ample natural light / floor-to-ceiling physics lounge windows' unverified; the 2013 photos do show a large glazed stair tower and big window bays. A UNH page in search results gives the original as 1913; the archives say 1914. No reviews found.
judgeNotes: Photos show a tidy contemporary block; no interior evidence or student reviews, so interior and reputation sit at mid-scale.
